'''Christie Jayaratnam Eliezer''' ({{langx|ta|கிரிஸ்டி ஜெயரத்தினம் எலியேசர்|translit=Kirisṭi Jeyarattiṉam Eliyēcar}}; 12 June 1918 &ndash; 10 March 2001) was a [[Ceylon Tamil]] mathematician, physicist and academic.

==Early life and family==
Eliezer was born on 12 June 1918 in [[Navatkuli]] in northern [[British Ceylon|Ceylon]].<ref name="Arumugam">{{cite book|last=Arumugam|first=S.|title=Dictionary of Biography of the Tamils of Ceylon|url=http://noolaham.net/project/19/1810/1810.pdf|year=1997|page=52|authorlink=S. Arumugam}}</ref><ref name="EAS">{{cite web|title=Eliezer, Christie Jayaratnam (1918 - 2001)|url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004528b.htm|publisher=Encyclopedia of Australian Science}}</ref> He was the son of Jacob Richard Eliezer and Elizabeth Ponnammah Vairakiam.<ref name="Arumugam"/> Both of his parents died when he was young.<ref name="Sangam">{{cite web|last1=Sri Kantha|first1=Sachi|authorlink1=Sachi Sri Kantha|title=Christie Jayaratnam Eliezer (1918-2001)|url=http://www.sangam.org/2012/07/Prof_CJ_Eliezer.php?uid=4791|publisher=Ilankai Tamil Sangam|date=14 July 2012}}</ref> Eliezer was educated at the Wesleyan Mission School, [[Puloly]] and [[Hartley College]], [[Point Pedro]] (1926–33) where he passed the Cambridge Local Examinations with honours and distinction.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="Sangam"/><ref name="TT0401">{{cite journal|last1=Senewiratne|first1=Brian|title=Professor C J Eliezer|journal=[[Tamil Times]]|date=15 April 2001|volume=XX|issue=4|pages=27–29|url=http://noolaham.net/project/36/3600/3600.pdf|issn=0266-4488}}</ref> He then spent a year studying at [[St. Joseph's College, Colombo]] before joining [[Ceylon University College]] in 1935, graduating with a first class honours [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] special degree in mathematics.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="TT0401"/><ref>{{cite book|title=Ceylon University College Prospectus 1936-37|year=1936|publisher=[[Ceylon University College]]|url=http://noolaham.net/project/66/6594/6594.pdf|page=43}}</ref>

Eliezer married Ranee, daughter of Rev. John Handy.<ref name="Arumugam"/> They had five children (Dhamayanthi, Ratna, Anandhi, Renuka and Tamara).<ref name="Arumugam"/>

==Career==
Eliezer worked at Ceylon University College as a [[visiting lecturer]] in 1938 before proceeding to [[Christ's College, Cambridge]] (1939–43) on a [[scholarship]] to study mathematics and [[theoretical physics]].<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="TT0401"/> He received a first class mathematics [[tripos]] from Christ's College in 1941.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="TT0401"/> He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree from Cambridge in 1946 after producing a [[thesis]], supervised by [[Paul Dirac]], on spinning electron and electromagnetic field.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="Sangam"/><ref name="TT0401"/><ref name="IAS">{{cite web|title=Christie Jayaratnam Eliezer|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/christie-jayaratnam-eliezer|publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]]}}</ref><ref name="LTU">{{cite web|title=Emeritus Professors|url=http://www.latrobe.edu.au/academicboard/emeritus-professors|publisher=[[La Trobe University]]}}</ref> Returning to Ceylon Eliezer lectured at the [[University of Ceylon]] for a brief period before rejoining Christ's College as a [[fellow]] (1946–49).<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> He received a [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] degree in 1949.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="LTU"/> He was [[called to the bar]] at the [[Middle Temple]] in 1949.<ref name="EAS"/><ref name="LTU"/>

Eliezer was appointed professor of mathematics at University of Ceylon in 1949.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> During his ten years at the university he was dean of the Faculty of Science from 1954 to 1957 and deputy pro-vice chancellor in 1955.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> Eliezer was a scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1955 to 1956, working with [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]].<ref name="TT0401"/><ref name="IAS"/> He spent some time at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="TT0401"/> Following the passing of the [[Sinhala Only Act]] in 1956, [[Sinhalese nationalists]] at the University of Ceylon, led by [[vice-chancellor]] [[Nicholas Attygalle]] and chancellor [[Dudley Senanayake]], attempted to remove [[Tamil language|Tamil]] as a [[medium of instruction]] at the university but this was thwarted by Eliezer and [[A. M. A. Azeez]], a member of the university's [[University council|council]].<ref name="TT0401"/>

Eliezer was appointed foundation professor of mathematics at the [[University of Malaya]] in 1959.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> The appointment was only meant be for two years but the deteriorating situation in Ceylon meant that Eliezer decided to stay in [[Federation of Malaya|Malaya]].<ref name="TT0401"/> During his nine years at the university he was dean of the Faculty of Science from 1959 to 1963 and deputy principal and vice-chancellor for another three years.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/> Eliezer became the first professor of applied mathematics at [[La Trobe University]] in 1968.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> During his 15 years at the university he was dean of the School of Physical Sciences (1969–71 and 1982–83) and deputy vice-chancellor for a period.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/> After retiring in 1983 he was appointed [[emeritus professor]] at La Trobe.<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="EAS"/><ref name="LTU"/>

Eliezer had been president of the Ceylon Association for the Advancement of Science.<ref name="IAS"/> He was a [[Fellow of the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]].<ref name="LTU"/> He received an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] D.Sc.Inf. degree from the [[University of Jaffna]] in 1981.<ref name="IAS"/><ref name="LTU"/> He was made a [[Member of the Order of Australia]] in 1996.<ref name="EAS"/><ref name="TT0401"/><ref name="IAS"/> He was awarded the [[Maamanithar]] (Great Man) honour by the rebel [[Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam]] on 19 October 1997.<ref name="Sangam"/><ref name="TT0401"/><ref name="IAS"/>

Eliezer was vice-president of the [[Colombo]] branch of the [[Young Men’s Christian Association]] and a member of the [[Jaffna College]] board.<ref name="Arumugam"/> He was president of the Ceylon Tamil Association of Victoria and chairman of the Australian Federation of Tamil Associations (1984-2001).<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="IAS"/> Eliezer helped Tamil refugees fleeing to Australia following the 1983  anti-Tamil [[Black July]] riots.<ref name="TT0401"/> He co-hosted a Tamil language programme on the [[Special Broadcasting Service]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Christie Jayaratnam Eliezer (12 June 1918 – 10 March 2001)|url=http://www.sbs.com.au/yourlanguage/tamil/en/content/christie-jayaratnam-eliezer-12-june-1918-10-march-2001|publisher=[[Special Broadcasting Service]]|date=9 June 2014}}</ref> Eliezer died on 10 March 2001 in [[Melbourne]].<ref name="EAS"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Eliezer Has Passed Away!|url=http://www.hartleycollege.com/eliezer/|publisher=[[Hartley College]]}}</ref>

==Works==
Eliezer wrote several books and articles including:<ref name="Arumugam"/><ref name="Sangam"/><ref name="TT0401"/>
* ''Concise Vector Analysis'' (1963, [[Pergamon Press]])
* ''A Modern Text-book on Statics: For Students of Applied Mathematics, Physics and Engineering'' (1964, Pergamon Press)
* ''Mathematics : Queen of the Arts, Handmaiden of the Sciences'' (1969, La Trobe University)
* ''The First Integrals of Some Differential Equations of Dynamics'' (1978, La Trobe University)
* ''Mechanics for Year Eleven'' (1988, co-author J. G. Barton)
